title: Comparison count of the timed median of three
statement: Let $a$, $b$, $c$ be elements of a linear order, and let $\mathrm{median3}(a,b,c)$ be the timed computation that returns a median of the three by a nested sequence of comparisons, charging one unit of time for each comparison performed. Then the recorded time cost of $\mathrm{median3}(a,b,c)$ is at most $3$; that is, the computation performs at most three comparisons.
hypotheses_covered: a, b, c are elements of a linear order
replaced:
The computation $\mathrm{median3}\,a\,b\,c$ records a time cost of at most $3$, i.e.\ it performs
at most three comparisons.
